Welcome to St Peter’s Church of England Primary School, Tunbridge Wells
At St Peter’s, we are proud to be a nurturing and inclusive school community where every child is known, valued, and encouraged to shine. Whether you are a current parent or considering joining our school family, we warmly welcome you.
Rooted in our Christian values of courage, compassion, and respect, we strive to create a learning environment where children feel safe, inspired, and empowered to be their very best. Our dedicated staff, supportive families, and enthusiastic pupils work together to make St Peter’s a truly special place to grow and learn. We invite you to explore our website to discover more about our vibrant school life, and how we are Learning to Light the Way—together.

New Starters
Admission Procedures for starting school in our reception class (children aged 4-5)
St Peter’s CE Primary School admits up to 30 children into our Reception Class in the academic year of their fifth birthday. In keeping with our vision—Learning to Light the Way—we aim to ensure that every child’s transition into school is nurturing and inclusive. All children joining St Peter’s are invited to induction events during the summer term, giving them the opportunity to meet their teacher, build confidence and become familiar with their new surroundings. To support this further, our Reception teacher also visits each child in their pre‑school setting, helping us to understand every child as a unique individual from the very beginning.
You will be advised of your school place on Thursday 16th April 2026. If you have been offered a place at St Peter’s, we will contact you with our welcome information on 20th April 2026. Please accept or decline your child’s place by emailing us at admissions@st-peters.kent.sch.uk no later than Thursday 30th April 2026, and include proof of address as outlined by Kent County Council. For further guidance, please refer to:
After you get your school offer – Kent County Council.
After you have accepted your place, you will receive full details of our summer‑term transition events, where children will have several opportunities to visit the school, explore our setting and get to know the adults who will support them. During the summer term, the Headteacher and Reception teacher also host an information meeting for parents and carers, offering practical guidance about school routines, uniform, and the work of our PTA, as well as time to ask questions.
If you feel it would be helpful to meet with our school SENCO prior to your child starting in September, please contact 01892 525727 to arrange an appointment during the summer term.
All applications must be completed online via Primary School Places – Kent County Council. The Local Authority coordinates the admissions process and will inform parents in writing of their outcome. At every stage, we aim to ensure that our procedures reflect our commitment to welcoming families with openness, kindness and clarity—shining a light on the values that underpin our school.
If you have any further questions, please email admissions@st-peters.kent.sch.uk

Wrap Around Care at St Peter's
wrap around charges 1 .pdf
Breakfast Club
Do your kids like a fun, energetic start to their day? Our Breakfast Club is open from 7:30 am every morning, and we’d love to welcome new faces! Whether your child enjoys games, crafts, or just a friendly chat over breakfast, there’s something here for everyone.
We know mornings can be busy, so let us help take the pressure off.
At Breakfast Club, students get a healthy meal and the chance to relax, play, and get ready for a great day at school.
It’s a wonderful way for children to make friends, try new activities, and arrive in class feeling happy and settled.
Spaces are open to all students. If you’d like to find out more or sign up, just contact the school office—we can’t wait to see your child at Breakfast Club!
Milky Way After School Club
Open every weekday from school finish until 6:00PM
Milky Way After School Club offers a warm, welcoming space for children from St. Peter’s CEP to relax, play, and explore after the school day ends. Whether your child joins us straight from class or arrives after another club like Football or Lego Club, they’ll be greeted with friendly familiar faces and plenty of exciting activities to dive into. Milky Way Club is run by teaching and support staff from St Peter’s school, which supports the children with the transition at the end of the day.
A World of Fun and Creativity
Our club is designed to spark imagination and encourage active play. Outdoors, children can enjoy the full-size football pitch, shoot hoops on the basketball court, or challenge friends to a game of badminton. The climbing apparatus and swingball setup are always popular, and croquet on the lawn adds a touch of classic fun. Hide and seek is a regular favourite, giving children the chance to run, laugh, and explore.
Indoors, the fun continues with a wide variety of games and creative stations. Children can play table football, pool, mini air hockey, and table tennis, or settle down with puzzles and board games. For those who love building and designing, we offer construction bricks and Minecraft-style blocks; a firm favourite for all ages. Our arts and crafts area is often buzzing with activity, and recent favourites include making loom band bracelets and keyrings.
We also host cooking sessions where children can make their own pizzas and cupcakes; a delicious way to learn new skills and enjoy a treat. And when it’s time to let loose on those dark winter evenings our disco and karaoke machine brings the party to life!
Film night and popcorn is a once a week treat at the end of the week when everyone is ready to relax.
Tasty and Healthy Snacks
To keep energy levels up, we provide a selection of healthy snacks each afternoon at 4:30pm. Children can enjoy, wraps with fillings of cheese, ham and salami, pitta bread and houmous dips, rice cakes, olives, fresh fruit, crackers, and breadsticks, perfect for refuelling between activities. The children sit down together at a table during snack time and enjoy a social chat, snack time is a favourite time, for sure! All staff are First Aid trained and club leaders are Level 2 Food Safety and Hygiene trained.
Easy Booking & Capacity Info
Bookings for Milky Way After School Club can be made through the Arbor App until 12:00 PM on the same day. We recommend booking early, as spaces can fill quickly, especially on busy days.
If the app doesn’t allow you to book, it may mean the club is already full for that day. Please do not hesitate to call the office should you have any questions regarding booking.
Transition from Other Clubs
Children attending other after-school clubs, such as Football Club or Lego Club are welcome to come straight to Milky Way After School Club afterwards. We’ll make sure they’re safely signed in and can join the fun as soon as their other club finishes.
Why Choose Milky Way?
Milky Way After School Club is more than just childcare, it’s a place where children can make friends, try new things, and enjoy their afternoons in a safe, familiar, supervised environment. With a wide variety of activities, flexible scheduling, and a caring team, we’re here to support busy families and give children a space to thrive. In addition to this, it provides a convenient childcare for busy families.

Languages - Spanish
At St Peter’s C of E Primary School, we aim to provide all of our children with a high-quality education in Foreign Languages, which develops their love of learning about other languages and cultures. Our current language taught is Spanish; however, we strive to provide children with opportunities to experience a range of other languages. We aim to ensure that by the end of our children’s primary education, they have acquired an understanding of both spoken and written Spanish, the confidence to speak in Spanish with others, and know how important other languages can be in their future.

What children at St Peter’s say about Spanish at our school:
“It is my favourite language that I have learnt at school”.
“It is my favourite subject; it is easy and interesting!”
“I love it, it is interesting to learn all the different phrases in another language”.
“It is helping me to speak with my family that are Spanish”.
“It is so easy, and I really enjoy it as it is brand new, and I can speak Spanish on holiday now!”
“I find it so fun, and it is so nice to learn about all the different languages and cultures around the world. I like that I can speak to my mum in Spanish and tell her all the new things I have learnt!”
Intent
St Peter’s CEP School intends to use the Language Angels scheme of work and resources to ensure we offer a relevant, broad, vibrant and ambitious foreign languages curriculum that will inspire and excite our pupils using a wide variety of topics and themes. All pupils will be expected to achieve their full potential by encouraging high expectations and excellent standards in their foreign language learning - the ultimate aim being that pupils will feel willing and able to continue studying languages beyond key stage 2.
The intent is that all content will be continuously updated and reviewed annually, creating a dynamic programme of study that will be clearly outlined in both long-term and short-term planning. This will ensure that the foreign language knowledge of our pupils progresses within each academic year and is extended year upon year throughout the primary phase and, in so doing, will always be relevant and in line with meeting or exceeding national DfE requirements.
The four key language learning skills; listening, speaking, reading and writing will be taught and all necessary grammar will be covered in an age-appropriate way across the primary phase. This will enable pupils to use and apply their learning in a variety of contexts, laying down solid foundations for future language learning and also helping the children improve overall attainment in other subject areas. In addition, the children will be taught how to look up and research language they are unsure of and they will have a bank of reference materials to help them with their spoken and written tasks going forward. This bank of reference materials will develop into a reference library to help pupils recall and build on previous knowledge throughout their primary school language learning journey.
The intent is that all pupils will develop a genuine interest and positive curiosity about foreign languages, finding them enjoyable and stimulating. Learning a second language will also offer pupils the opportunity to explore relationships between language and identity, develop a deeper understanding of other cultures and the world around them with a better awareness of self, others and cultural differences. The intention is that they will be working towards becoming life-long language learners.
Implementation of our Foreign Languages Curriculum at St Peter’s
All classes will have access to a very high-quality foreign language curriculum using the Language Angels scheme of work and resources. This will progressively develop pupil skills in foreign languages through regularly taught and well-planned weekly lessons in KS2 which will be taught by class teachers.
Children will progressively acquire, use and apply a growing bank of vocabulary, language skills and grammatical knowledge organised around age-appropriate topics and themes - building blocks of language into more complex, fluent and authentic language.
All teachers will know where every child is at any point in their foreign language learning journey.
The planning of different levels of challenge (as demonstrated in the various Language Angels Teaching Type categories) and which units to teach at each stage of the academic year will be addressed dynamically and will be reviewed in detail annually as units are updated and added to the scheme. Lessons offering appropriate levels of challenge and stretch will be taught at all times to ensure pupils learn effectively, continuously building their knowledge of and enthusiasm for the language(s) they are learning.
Language Angels are categorised by ‘Teaching Type’ to make it easier for teachers to choose units that will offer the appropriate level of challenge and stretch for the classes they are teaching.
Early Language units are entry-level units and are most appropriate for KS1 and Year 3 pupils or pupils with little or no previous foreign language learning. Intermediate units increase the level of challenge by increasing the amount and complexity (including foreign language grammar concepts) of the foreign language presented to pupils. Intermediate units are suitable for Year 4-5 pupils or pupils with embedded basic knowledge of the foreign language. Progressive and Creative Curriculum units are the most challenging units and are suitable for Year 6 pupils or pupils with a good understanding of the basics of the language they are learning. Grouping units into these Teaching Type categories ensures that the language taught is appropriate to the level of the class and introduced when the children are ready. Children will be taught how to listen and read longer pieces of text gradually in the foreign language, and they will have ample opportunities to speak, listen to, read and write the language being taught with and without scaffolds, frames and varying levels of support.
Early Language Units (entry-level) and Core Vocabulary lessons are designed to run for approximately 30 minutes. Intermediate, Progressive and Creative Curriculum units are designed to run for approximately 45 minutes.
Units, where possible and appropriate, will be linked to class topics and cross-curricular themes. Children will build on previous knowledge gradually as their foreign language lessons continue to recycle, revise and consolidate previously learnt language whilst building on all four language skills: listening, speaking, reading and writing. Knowledge and awareness of required and appropriate grammar concepts will be taught throughout all units at all levels of challenge. Teachers are provided with a Progression Map and Grammar Grid (downloadable from the “Curriculum Guidance” area of the Language Angels website) to ensure all children are progressing in their foreign language learning skills and are taught the appropriate grammar at the right time in their foreign language learning journey. Grammar rules and patterns will be taught by the level of challenge:
Grammar is integrated and taught discreetly throughout all appropriate units. Teachers can also use the specific Grammar Explained units to ensure pupils are exposed to all of the appropriate grammar, so they are able to create their own accurate and personalised responses to complex authentic foreign language questions by the end of the primary phase.
The Progression Map shows precisely how pupil foreign language learning across the key skills of speaking, listening, reading, writing and grammar progresses within each Language Angels ‘Teaching Type’ and also how the level of learning and progression of each pupil is increased as pupils move across each subsequently more challenging Language Angels ‘Teaching Type’. It is a visual demonstration of the progression that takes place WITHIN a ‘Teaching Type’ and also ACROSS each ‘Teaching Type’.
The school has a unit planner in place which will serve as an overall ‘teaching map’ outlining for all teachers within the school what each class in each year group will be taught and when it will be taught. Each class in each year group will have an overview of units to be taught during the academic year to ensure substantial progress and learning is achieved. Each teaching unit is divided into 6 fully planned lessons.
Units are progressive within themselves as subsequent lessons within a unit build on the language and knowledge taught in previous lessons. As pupils progress through the lessons in a unit they will build their knowledge and develop the complexity of the language they use. We think of the progression within the 6 lessons in a unit as ‘language Lego’. We provide blocks of language knowledge and, over the course of a 6-week unit, encourage pupils to build more complex and sophisticated language structures with their blocks of language knowledge.
Pupil learning and progression will be assessed at regular intervals in line with school policy. Teachers will aim to assess each language skill (speaking, listening, reading and writing) twice throughout each scholastic year to be able to provide reference points against which learning and progression in each skill can be demonstrated.
In addition to following the lessons provided in the Language Angels scheme of work and resources, teachers are encouraged to also do some of the following:
Foreign language celebration assemblies.
Inclusion
All pupils throughout the school, shall have the opportunity to develop foreign language capability. The school promotes equal opportunities and fairness of distribution of foreign language resources. Children with other languages at home are encouraged to use them for educational benefit and parents are offered advice about what is appropriate. Efforts are made to ensure that languages used at home are highlighted in the classroom once a teacher has been notified.
French Club
Our weekly French Club for Years 1-3 and 4-6 is run by 'La Jolie Ronde', an award-winning provider of French language learning for children. Our French Club encourages children to become confident and enthusiastic language learners and helps to provide them with a skill for life. Children attending the club benefit from a structured and progressive program and, over time, begin to speak, read and write independently.

Clubs
Extra-Curricular Activities
At St Peter’s, we provide a broad selection of extra‑curricular clubs, run by both our own staff and trusted external specialists. You can find full details of which clubs take place on each day in our Autumn Term 2026 schedule:/docs/CLUBS_Term_1_2_2026.docx
If you’d like a clearer picture of what each club offers, please continue reading below.
Athletics club (Delivered by West Kent Athletics Club)
Athletics Club at St Peter’s is delivered by West Kent Athletics Club and gives KS2 pupils a fast‑paced, skills‑focused introduction to the sport. Sessions are built around fun games and technique‑based activities that develop running, jumping and throwing skills in an engaging, age‑appropriate way. Children learn correct form, improve coordination and build confidence through challenges and team‑based tasks, making it an energetic club where older pupils can enjoy progressing their athletic ability while staying active. Click here for more information and to sign up via their website: West Kent Athletics Club
Choir
The school choir is a welcoming group for pupils who enjoy singing and performing together. Children learn a range of songs, develop vocal confidence, and practise essential musical skills such as harmony, rhythm, and teamwork. The choir regularly prepares pieces for school events and celebrations, giving members the chance to shine and share their hard work with the wider community.
Creative writing club
Creative Writing Club gives KS2 pupils the chance to stretch their imagination and develop their storytelling skills. Each session explores different writing styles, prompts and techniques, helping children craft characters, build worlds and experiment with language. Older pupils are encouraged to refine their ideas, share their work and offer supportive feedback, building confidence as young authors while enjoying a space dedicated to creativity.
Dance club (Delivered by Trinity Dance School)
Dance Club at St Peter’s is run by Trinity Dance and welcomes all children from Years 1–6. The sessions are energetic, inclusive and designed to help pupils learn fun routines, take part in creative dance games and build confidence in their movement skills. Children develop coordination, musicality and technique while enjoying a supportive environment where new starters and all abilities are encouraged. With performance opportunities throughout the year, pupils get the chance to showcase their hard work and celebrate their progress as young dancers. Click here for more information and to sign up via their website: St Peter's Primary Dance Club (Term 1) - Booking by Bookwhen
Drawing club
Drawing Club offers a relaxed, supportive space where children can explore different artistic techniques at their own pace. Each session uses tailor‑made videos and creative prompts to guide pupils through step‑by‑step activities, ensuring every child feels confident and included. Whether experimenting with new styles or developing their own ideas, children are encouraged to enjoy the process, express themselves and build their drawing skills week by week.
Drama club (Delivered by Zylo Drama School)
Drama Club at St Peter’s is delivered by Zylo Drama School and offers children in Years 2–6 a lively, confidence‑building introduction to performance. Through games, improvisation, storytelling and character work, pupils develop key skills such as teamwork, creativity, vocal expression and stage presence. Sessions are designed to be fun, supportive and highly engaging, helping children grow in confidence while learning how to communicate clearly, collaborate with others and bring stories to life. Click here for more information and to sign up via their website: Performing Arts Clubs For Kids in Brighton | Zylo Performance
Football clubs (Delivered by EMC)
Football Club at St Peter’s is run by EMC Coaching and gives children a high‑quality, energetic introduction to playing “the EMC way.” Each session is split into two groups — Years 1–3 and Years 4–6 — ensuring coaching is age‑appropriate and engaging for all pupils. Children develop core football skills such as passing, shooting, defending, ball manipulation, 1v1 play and teamwork, all within a fun, supportive environment led by fully qualified coaches. Pupils also enjoy small‑sided matches and structured challenges that help build confidence, game understanding and a love of the sport.
Film club
Film Club is a gentle, age‑appropriate introduction to watching and talking about movies for children in KS1. Pupils enjoy short, engaging films and animated stories chosen to suit younger viewers, helping them develop listening skills, imagination and early discussion skills. Each session includes simple conversations about characters, settings and favourite moments, making it a calm and enjoyable end‑of‑day activity for our youngest learners.
Gardening club (Autumn and Summer terms only)
Gardening Club gives KS2 pupils the chance to learn practical outdoor skills while helping to care for the school grounds. Running only in the autumn and summer terms, children take part in seasonal activities such as planting, weeding, watering and harvesting, gaining hands‑on experience of how plants grow and change throughout the year. It’s an enjoyable, active club that encourages responsibility, teamwork and a love of nature.
Gymnastics (Delivered by Gymspire)
Gymnastics Club at St Peter’s is delivered by Gymspire Academy and is open to all children across the school. Their sessions are active, engaging and carefully structured to help pupils develop strength, coordination, balance and confidence through a wide range of gymnastics activities. Children learn skills progressively in a fun, supportive environment, with coaches tailoring sessions so every child can take part, challenge themselves and enjoy moving. Click here for more information and to sign up via their website: Tunbridge Wells | Gymspire Academy
Homework club
Homework Club provides a calm, supportive space where pupils can complete their assignments with guidance from staff. Children can work independently or ask for help when needed, ensuring they understand tasks and stay on top of their learning. It’s also a great opportunity to develop good study habits in a relaxed, structured environment.
Judo club (Delivered by Bushido Judo)
Judo Club at St Peter’s is delivered by Bushido Judo School and offers children from Years 1–6 a dynamic, high‑energy introduction to this Olympic martial art. Sessions blend fun multi‑skills activities with core judo techniques, helping pupils develop agility, balance, coordination and overall fitness. Alongside the physical skills, children learn important values such as respect, discipline, self‑control and fair play, building resilience and confidence in a supportive environment. It’s an exciting, hands‑on club where pupils can be active, have fun and discover the foundations of judo. Click here for more information and to sign up via their website: Schools | Bushido Judo
Lego club
Lego Club gives children the chance to get creative with bricks while tackling fun weekly building challenges. Each session encourages imagination, problem‑solving, and teamwork as pupils design and construct models based on a new theme or task. It’s a lively, hands‑on club where children can share ideas, experiment with different builds, and proudly showcase their creations at the end of each week.
Sewing club (Delivered by The Little Sewing School)
Sewing Club at St Peter’s is run by The Little Sewing School and gives KS2 children a fun, hands‑on introduction to using a sewing machine. Pupils learn how to thread and operate the machine safely through simple starter projects, gradually building confidence before moving on to more challenging creations. Each term features exciting makes such as wallets, messenger bags, donut cushions, oodies and seasonal bunting, allowing children to develop practical skills while enjoying the satisfaction of producing something unique and handmade. Click on this link for more information and to book a spot: School Clubs — The Little Sewing School
Yoga and Mindful colouring (KS1 Only)
Yoga and Mindful Colouring Club offers KS1 children a calm, nurturing space to unwind at the end of the day. Pupils take part in simple yoga stretches and breathing exercises designed to help them relax, followed by gentle colouring activities that encourage focus and creativity. The combination supports emotional wellbeing, helping younger children feel settled, centred and ready for the rest of their afternoon.
